extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant applicants / PIs and others who follow NIH peer review outcomes
extracted.subtask_description: Explains recent NIH study section triage/streamlining changes: larger fraction of applications are marked Not Discussed (ND) and a new “Not Discussed, but Competitive” label for a subset; describes how these designations appear in eRA Commons and the administrative workflow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Triage/streamlining rules (ND rate)
rubrics_metrics.description: Previously, approximately half of proposals are Not Discussed at the meeting, based on the average of preliminary overall impact scores from the assigned reviewers. This has now been extended such that approximately 70% will Not be Discussed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The post frames this as a temporary adoption for the current and following rounds of NIH study section meetings. The practical effect is that a larger fraction of apps will be triaged out of full discussion based on preliminary overall impact score averages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis for ND (use of preliminary overall impact scores)
rubrics_metrics.description: Not Discussed (ND) decisions are made based on the average of preliminary overall impact scores from the assigned reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This identifies the measurable criterion used for triage — the reviewers' preliminary overall impact scores — rather than informal or non-scored reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: "Not Discussed, but Competitive" designation
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH has instituted a new “Not Discussed, but Competitive” designation for the ~middle third, i.e., the top half of the ND.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This label marks applications that were triaged (ND) but are considered competitive within the ND pool, allowing Program greater flexibility to pick up grants. The post notes the designation is appearing in eRA Commons later than the initial ND flag.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing/administrative workflow for ND vs Competitive flags in eRA Commons
rubrics_metrics.description: The first set of scores are being returned to PIs now and all of the ND proposals are first marked in eRA Commons as ND. The “Competitive” designation has been showing up a day to many days later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author reports that the SRO dashboard apparently only allows entry of ND; the SRO must then send their list of 'Competitive' NDs to an eRA Commons person who can make the adjustments. The post emphasizes this is an administrative sequencing issue, not post-meeting re‑sorting of lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose / likely permanence of changes (meeting length and section reductions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cutting meetings down to one day and getting through a larger set of apps assigned to one section will permit the reduction in total number of sections; the author is skeptical the change will be temporary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The post suggests institutional incentives (shorter meetings, fewer sections) make the triage/streamlining changes likely to persist, and that the 'competitive' ND supports Program flexibility to fund without full discussion.
